opportunities.title: Small grants

amount.raw: Awards generally fall in a range of £1,500-£5,000 and will only exceptionally exceed £6,000. Travel and subsistence up to £2,000 per person for trips up to 13 days, up to £2,500 per person for 14 days or more; up to £5,000 for PhD fieldwork visits of six months or more.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Applicants must belong to, or provide evidence of support from, an organisation or institution willing to receive grant funds. Applications are not accepted from individuals seeking support for personal projects, though the UK office may consider individuals with proof of organisational support. Projects originating in the UK should be submitted through the UK office. Not for undergraduate or master's students; PhD students may apply (with supervisor letter of support).
opportunities.summary: Seed funding to enable UK-Japan projects that might otherwise not be possible, bringing people in the UK and Japan together to deepen mutual understanding, exchange ideas or expertise, or develop lasting collaboration. Supports festivals, workshops, performances, exchanges, collaborative projects, Japanese language and cultural studies teaching, and academic research/visits/exchange.

opportunities.title: Butterfield Awards in Medicine and Health

amount.raw: Up to £10,000 per year; continuing projects lasting up to three years to a maximum of £10,000 per year, to a total limit of £30,000.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Applicants should normally be able to show an existing research record, but consideration is also given to practitioners, managers, carers or others in health-related fields. Projects must involve partners in both the UK and Japan. Preference given to those not previously involved in UK-Japan collaboration and early-career applicants. Apply to the UK office regardless of where based.
opportunities.summary: Supports exchanges and collaborations between health and medical professionals in Japan and the UK, including study of scientific, clinical, social and economic issues in healthcare. Grants may be used for travel expenses or to contribute to other costs including conference and publication costs.
